name: LOW POINTS
clue: Bathers bob like corks in this lake between Israel & Jordan, whose shore, about 1,400 feet below sea level, is Earth's lowest land

name: CORPS VALUES
clue: Sent by Jefferson to explore his vast new purchase, this pair & their Corps of Discovery reached the Pacific in 1805

name: BOXED IN
clue: In Hesiod, the gods crafted her as the first mortal woman; she unsealed a jar, loosing every ill but leaving hope inside

name: LANDLOCKED
clue: This South American country lost its Pacific coastline to Chile in an 1880s war, yet it still maintains a navy

name: EPIC TITLES
clue: Homer's epic of the Trojan War takes its title not from its hero but from this alternate name for Troy

name: WORTH ITS WEIGHT
clue: Harvested from crocus stigmas at roughly 150 flowers per gram, this spice has long rivaled gold as the world's costliest.

name: FINAL EPISODES
clue: Over 100 million Americans watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen,' the 1983 finale of this Korean War sitcom

name: BROADWAY RECORDS
clue: Running from 1988 to 2023, this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical logged Broadway's longest run at 13,981 performances

name: SUE-PERSTAR
clue: Named for the fossil hunter who spotted her in South Dakota in 1990, Sue is the Field Museum's $8.36 million specimen of this species

name: ORGAN RECITAL
clue: This human organ can regrow to full size from as little as a quarter of its original mass

name: THE MATH BEHIND PHYSICS
clue: Einstein praised this German mathematician, whose 1915 theorem tied every symmetry of nature to a conservation law.

name: GOING THE DISTANCE
clue: This event's exact 26-mile-385-yard length traces to the 1908 London Games' course, Windsor Castle to the royal box

name: IT'S ALL GREEK TO HER
clue: Egypt's last active pharaoh, she was a native Greek speaker descended from one of Alexander the Great's generals

name: AND THE OSCAR GOES TO...
clue: This 1969 tale of two New York hustlers is the only X-rated film ever to win the Best Picture Oscar

name: LANGUAGE ISOLATES
clue: Spoken in the western Pyrenees, this European language has no known living relatives anywhere in the world

name: MOLD RUSH
clue: Back from vacation in 1928, Alexander Fleming found a stray mold wiping out staph colonies, the source of this drug

name: FACE THE MUSIC
clue: At the 1824 premiere of his Ninth Symphony, a soloist turned this composer around so he could see the ovation he couldn't hear

name: CELL BIOLOGY
clue: These energy-producing organelles carry their own DNA, a genome you inherit only from your mother

name: A BRUSH WITH HISTORY
clue: Jacques-Louis David painted the 1793 death of this radical French journalist, stabbed in his medicinal bath by Charlotte Corday.

name: DRINK TO THAT
clue: Its melody began as 'To Anacreon in Heaven,' a London club's drinking tune; Congress made it official in 1931

name: LIGHT THE WAY
clue: Celebrating Rama's return to Ayodhya, this five-day autumn 'festival of lights' fills India with oil lamps and fireworks.

name: THE CONSTITUTION
clue: It's the only constitutional amendment ratified specifically to repeal an earlier amendment

name: PROOF POSITIVE
clue: In 1931 this Austrian logician's incompleteness theorems proved that arithmetic contains true statements no formal proof can reach.

name: LINES OF LATITUDE
clue: It's the only country on Earth crossed by both the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn

name: SIEGE THE DAY
clue: Homer's Iliad never mentions it; Virgil's Aeneid holds the most famous ancient account of this hollow ruse that ended a 10-year war

name: CEILING THE DEAL
clue: Protesting that painting was not his art, this sculptor of 'David' spent 4 years frescoing a ceiling for Pope Julius II

name: DYING DECLARATIONS
clue: Rivals turned pen pals, these 2 Founding Fathers died hours apart on July 4, 1826, their Declaration's 50th anniversary

name: STELLAR NEIGHBORS
clue: This red dwarf, with a name meaning 'nearest,' is the closest star to our sun

name: WAR PAINT
clue: At his request, this Spaniard's stark mural of a 1937 town bombing stayed at New York's MoMA until democracy returned to Spain

name: SCHOOL TIES
clue: Shakespeare enrolled this brooding prince at Wittenberg, the university town where Martin Luther posted his 95 theses
